title: Ring Unwrapping Slider with Side-by-Side Views

payload.learning_objective: See that when a thin ring is cut and unrolled, it becomes a rectangle with width equal to the circumference (2πr) and height equal to the ring thickness — and that these rectangles stack into a triangular shape

mini_spec.title: Ring Unwrapping Slider with Side-by-Side Views
mini_spec.manipulated_variable: A slider control that changes the number of rings the circle is divided into (from perhaps 3 to 50 rings)
mini_spec.primary_visual_feedback: The circle re-divides into more or fewer concentric rings, and simultaneously the stack of rectangles on the right updates to show correspondingly thinner or thicker rectangles, maintaining visual correspondence through color; the stacked rectangles form a stepped approximation to a triangle
mini_spec.goal_structure: Free exploration with implicit guidance toward increasing ring count to observe rectangles becoming more uniform in width and the triangle shape becoming cleaner
mini_spec.causal_chain_exposed: Each ring displays its radius value r, the corresponding rectangle shows its width labeled as 2πr, and its height labeled as dr; total area of rectangles displayed numerically approaching πr²
mini_spec.trace_strategy: None - the current state is sufficient because the concept focuses on the geometric transformation at the current subdivision level
mini_spec.aha_moment: Discovering that as rings get thinner (higher ring count), the stacked rectangles form a cleaner and cleaner triangle shape, with the widest rectangle at the top (outer circumference) and shortest at the bottom (inner rings)

payload.section_context: Second section, building on the rings from section 1. Students now see what happens when rings are cut open and laid flat.
payload.design_brief: This lesson derives the circle area formula πr² using concentric rings. The shared domain model includes: circumference at radius r = 2πr, ring area ≈ 2πr × dr, and the fact that stacked rings form a triangle with base 2πR and height R. This section shows the transformation from rings to rectangles and hints at the triangle shape. Use a side-by-side layout with circle on left and stacked strips on right.
payload.proposition: A thin ring, when cut and unrolled, becomes a rectangle with width 2πr (the circumference) and height dr (the thickness)
payload.narrative_draft:
Now for the key trick. Imagine taking scissors to one of those rings, snipping it open, and laying it flat on the table. What do you get? A thin rectangle.

The width of that rectangle is the circumference at that radius — 2πr. The height is just the thickness of the ring. Adjust the slider to change how many rings divide the circle. As you add more rings, each one gets thinner, and the stack of rectangles on the right shows a cleaner approximation of... something familiar.

Do you see it forming? The rectangles are arranging themselves into a shape you already know how to calculate.

contract.student_changes: adjusts the number of rings with a slider
contract.student_sees: strips become thinner and more numerous, forming a stepped triangle shape
